_readme: NAMED OWNERS FOR WORKFLOWS THAT ARE OFF THE PR PATH (task-dee226be3107a98b c4).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A workflow on the PR path has an owner by construction: the
person whose PR it reddens. Move it to `push: main` and that owner disappears --
it cannot block a merge, no PR ever surfaces it, and a lane's close-out reads its
own PRs, never main's health. posix-vacuous-green-census.yml failed on main's tip
for ELEVEN HOURS across EIGHT consecutive runs and cost nobody a second
(task-6005859f86872319). scripts/main-red-owner.sh answers 'somebody must be told';
this file answers 'WHO'. Without it the watcher's issue is addressed to the repo,
which is the same nobody one layer out.
THE INCIDENT WORKFLOW HAS NO ROW HERE ANY MORE, AND THAT IS THE GUARD WORKING.
posix-vacuous-green-census.yml was put BACK on the PR path on 2026-09-16 after the
same class recurred: 36 consecutive red census runs on main, from 9b9e26c23 onward,
for two freshly-landed unguarded scripts. On the PR path it has an owner by
construction again -- the author of the PR that adds the unguarded script -- so the
derived population no longer contains it, and workflow-owner-check.sh reds on a
STALE row for an on-PR workflow exactly as it reds on a MISSING row for an off-PR
one. It did, which is how this row came out.
AND AGAIN, 2026-09-17: pipefail-sigpipe-scan.yml. Its row said a per-PR run would
re-scan the tree 'to re-derive an unchanged verdict'. The verdict was not unchanged.
Off the PR path it failed on FIFTEEN consecutive pushes to main (50 of its last 100
push runs red) with 'RATCHET BROKEN -- 104 finding(s) at confidence >= high, baseline
is 101': three new sites had landed through PRs that never ran it, and every red
named an author who had not written them. Back on the PR path, so the row is gone and
the guard reds on the stale row -- which is how it came out (task-4f360efc26a428f5).
AND A THIRD, 2026-09-25: scaffy-catalog-drift.yml. Its row said the comparand IS
main, so on a PR it 'answers about the base, not the change'. False: seed --check
derives the CHECKED-OUT tree (on a PR, the merge commit) and compares it to the
served catalog, and seed --impact bills each drifted command to the PR's own changed
files. It now runs on pull_request as a pre-merge notice (never required), so the
row came out (task dr-w31-bl-served-catalog-drift-is-red-and-unowned).
THE POPULATION IS DERIVED, NEVER CURATED. A workflow belongs here iff it carries a
`push:` arm and NO `pull_request:` arm -- i.e. it is off the PR path, so only the
watcher can see its red. scripts/workflow-owner-check.sh recomputes that set from
the workflow files on every run and REFUSES when it does not match the keys below.
You cannot move a workflow off the PR path and forget this file: the guard reds.
`owner` IS A LANE, not a person. Lanes are the repo's own fence table (CLAUDE.md):
api, console, deploy, gates, cli, studio. A lane outlives any individual and is
the unit a close-out can actually be pointed at. `owner` must be one of those six.
`why_off_pr` IS LOAD-BEARING and is the one line the row demands for every move:
why the PR is the wrong place for this check, in a sentence a reader can dispute.
THE PREDICATE WIDENED ON 2026-09-18 (felix-w24-bl-workflows-ownership-gap).
It used to read `push: AND NOT pull_request:`, which is not the property that
matters -- it is one WAY of having it. A schedule-only workflow has no push arm
and no PR arm either, so the old predicate filed it under "on the PR path" and
the guard's own OK line then said, of all of them, "owned by their PR author".
That sentence was false about THIRTEEN of this repo's 78 workflows: nine cron'd
(paper-readers at 05:17Z, elixir-nightly at 03:17Z, absent-context-census every
six hours, ...), one workflow_run-driven (elixir-main-red-attribution), three
dispatch-only. The registry held 10 rows and the hole was 13.
OFF THE PR PATH NOW MEANS "CAN FAIL UNATTENDED": no `pull_request:` arm, AND at
least one of `push`, `schedule`, `workflow_run`, `release`. Still derived, still
recomputed every run.
DISPATCH-ONLY WORKFLOWS ARE OUT, BY RULE AND NOT BY NAME. cp-ops.yml,
deprecate.yml and retag.yml only start when a person presses the button, and
that person is reading the result -- the hole this file closes is a red NOBODY
SEES. The exclusion is the predicate (`workflow_dispatch` is not an unattended
arm), never a list: put a cron on any of the three tomorrow and the guard reds
for a missing row on that same commit.
WHICH WATCHER SEES WHICH. A push-armed row is read by
scripts/main-red-predicate.sh, which enumerates by push arm -- that is what
RED 5 is about, and RED 5 therefore fires only on push-armed rows. A cron'd row
is read by scripts/scheduled-arm-health.sh, which derives its own population
from every cron'd workflow in the tree. elixir-main-red-attribution.yml is read
by NEITHER (it is workflow_run-driven, with no push arm and no cron); its row
names an owner, and the visibility half of that one is an open corner, stated
here rather than implied by a clean guard.

absent-context-census.yml.why_off_pr: dates an ABSENCE across the whole open-PR population and the queue behind it -- a property of GitHub's run/check state at a moment in time, which no single diff changes and no PR head can reproduce.

cli-release-cadence.yml.why_off_pr: asks whether the RELEASE CADENCE has slipped -- a property of the tag history over time, not of any one diff; a PR cannot make it true or false.

cli-release.yml.why_off_pr: publishes a release from a tag; running it on a PR head would cut artifacts from unmerged code.

codebase-intel.yml.why_off_pr: re-learns the scoring weights from the codebase's whole incident history on release and on a Monday cron; a PR head is one point in that history, not the subject.

deploy.yml.why_off_pr: ships merged code to real hosts; a PR head must never reach a box.

elixir-main-red-attribution.yml.why_off_pr: answers 'did the PR that landed this actually RUN the test main just failed on' -- it is triggered BY the main elixir run completing, so the event it reports on does not exist on a PR.

elixir-nightly.yml.why_off_pr: runs the ELEVEN tags test_helper.exs excludes from every PR and main push; putting that cost on each PR is the reason they are excluded in the first place.

grip-suite.yml.why_off_pr: the Grip ledger suite reads durable ledger state, not the diff; on a PR it measures the same thing every time at full cost.

landed-mark.yml.why_off_pr: records that a PR LANDED -- the event it reports does not exist until the merge commit does.

landed-open-report.yml.why_off_pr: walks the ledger for rows whose work merged and never closed -- a slowly-moving population in Barkpark, not a fact about any diff.

paper-readers.yml.why_off_pr: inventories the LIVE production Paper corpus, which production can change without touching this repository, so a PR green would say nothing about it.

pds-scratch-round-trip.yml.why_off_pr: boots a real scratch Postgres target, verifies and tears it down; it is a live-infrastructure round trip, not something a PR runner should be starting per push.

release-artifact.yml.why_off_pr: builds and uploads release artifacts for a pushed ref.

release-curator-draft.yml.why_off_pr: opens or refreshes a draft Release once main has settled and CI on that head is green; the head it needs is main's, not the PR's.

release.yml.why_off_pr: cuts the release itself; tag-shaped, not diff-shaped.

renew-mail-cert.yml.why_off_pr: renews the mail.barkpark.cloud LE cert via DNS-01 and reloads postfix on the CP box -- a monthly real-world side effect that must never fire from a PR head.

scheduled-arm-health.yml.why_off_pr: reads every cron'd workflow's real scheduled-run history against GitHub; its subject is run history, which no diff changes, and on a PR it would cost ~90 gh api calls to re-derive an unchanged verdict.

seal-reading.yml.why_off_pr: seals a reading over landed history; nothing is sealed until the commit is on main.

twoslash.yml.why_off_pr: type-checks docs snippets against the PUBLISHED SDK surface, which only changes on a release.
